newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-NORTHERN IRELAND FRUSTRATE GERMANS AT HOME.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NORTHERN IRELAND FRUSTRATE GERMANS AT HOME.

text.p: Northern Ireland frustrated Germany's World Cup qualifying campaign when they held the European champions to a 1-1 draw in a group nine qualifier on Saturday.

The Germans, who have now not beaten Northern Ireland in five matches since 1977, had to come back from behind after defender Gerry Taggart gave the visitors the lead against the run of play with a well-taken goal in the 39th minute.
Midfielder Andy Moeller scored a superb individual effort two minutes later to equalise, but from then on Berti Vogts's team failed to find a way through the province's packed defence.

Northern Ireland 'keeper Tommy Wright, playing his first international for two years, had a superb match. Luck was not on the Germans' side at all. Captain Juergen Klinsmann saw a second-half header hit both posts before bouncing into Wright's arms.

"When I saw that I knew we wouldn't win it," Vogts said. "The goalkeeper had a great day. We had chances but luck was not on our side. But you get games like this...We are still optimistic about qualifying for (the finals in) France."
Northern Ireland, who played very defensively, surprised the Germans tactically by playing with a sweeper at the back.

The European champions put the visitors under intense pressure in the first half an hour. But Wright dived low to stop defender Markus Babbel's close-range header early on and tipped a spectacular long-range shot from wing-back Michael Tarnat over the bar in the 26th minute.

The Northern Ireland goal came completely against the run of play. German midfielder Thomas Strunz gave the ball away to Taggart on the right hand side of the box. The Bolton defender struck it hard into the left-hand corner with his left foot.
The visiting fans were still celebrating the goal when Moeller equalised with a crisp right-footed strike into the top right-hand corner.
The Germans piled on the pressure again at the start of the second half. But Wright reacted quickly to stop a Moeller header in the 57th minute.

Eight minutes later the Germans had their closest chance of the match when a Klinsmann header hit the left-hand post and then bounced across the line to hit the right post before bouncing into Wright's arms.
Northern Ireland had previously taken just one point from their first two qualifiers.
But the Germans, who have lost just one World Cup qualifier in their entire history, have struggled against them since they thrashed them 5-0 in Cologne in 1977.
Northern Ireland have now drawn three and won two of their last five encounters against the Euro 96 champions.
